units.note: Chapter ends mid-sentence (εἰς ἑκάτερον τῶν προειρημένων | ἁμαρτημάτων ἐμπίπτουσι in ch. 48); English completes the clause here, which is a seam, not a lacuna.

findings.quote: because they take their initial premises to be false and irrational
findings.problem: διὰ τὸ τὰς πρώτας ὑποθέσεις ψευδεῖς καὶ παραλόγους λαμβάνειν = because they adopt initial premises that are false and irrational. The English says the playwrights regard their premises as false, which is not the sense: they adopt false premises without knowing it.
findings.proposed_fix: because the initial premises they adopt are false and irrational

units.note: [τοὐναντίον] in 48.3 is bracketed (deleted) by the editor; English rightly ignores it.

findings.quote: to join in helping him secure the throne, he agreed,
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna marked *** between συμπεριποιῆσαι τὴν ἀρχὴν αὐτῷ and ὑπήκουσε; the English reads straight on as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: to join in helping him secure the throne, [...] he agreed,

units.note: Smoothed lacuna only; numbers (three days, four days) and names (Publius, his brother, Rhone, Isère, Allobroges) check out.
